transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is I keep making these small mistakes that end up being really embarrassing. Like I’ll turn in an application or some research notes and later notice I mislabeled an artwork date or skipped a question, even though I really thought I had checked it.

It’s not like I’m trying to rush, either—well, sometimes I guess I am, but even when I slow down and look it over, something slips through. And then I feel kind of ridiculous, because it’s usually such a tiny thing, but it makes the whole thing look careless.
Do you often find your mind drifting away when you’re doing detailed tasks?

Yeah, pretty often. Especially if I’m at my desk trying to read or write something detailed. Like, I’ll be working through a paragraph and then a siren goes by outside, or I hear someone talking in the hallway, and suddenly I’m listening to that instead.

Or sometimes it’s not even something outside—it’ll be some random thought, like an idea for an exhibit layout or an artwork I saw once, and then I kind of follow that thread. And then, I don’t know, twenty minutes can go by before I realize I’m not doing the thing I sat down to do.
Do you remember having this same kind of distractibility and careless mistakes when you were a child, such as in grade school?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I was a decent student, so it didn’t look like I was totally checked out, but even in elementary school my teachers would write stuff like, “good ideas,” or “creative,” and then also that I forgot to turn in worksheets or didn’t follow all the instructions.

My parents used to check my backpack every night, which was this whole routine—folders, crumpled papers, random permission slips—and if they didn’t, I’d lose things or miss some tiny detail. I remember thinking it was unfair because I knew the material, but then I’d skip a question or forget the sheet existed.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work because you feel driven to make sure it’s exactly right?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do check things, but I don’t know if it feels like… driven, exactly. Sometimes I’ll reread something because I know I miss details, but then I can still miss them, which is frustrating.

“Exactly right” makes me think of, like, lining up labels in a gallery or getting the spacing right on a wall text—sorry, that’s kind of a random example—but with my own work it’s more like I’m trying not to overlook something obvious. I don’t think I’m checking over and over because it has to be perfect, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t know if I’d call it excessive. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I think—school, or work plans, or whether I forgot something. Actually, “forgot something” is probably the one that pops up more, like when I’m leaving somewhere and I pat all my pockets, which is maybe just a habit.

But a lot of different things for no reason… I’m not sure. I don’t think I’m constantly worrying all day. Sometimes my mind jumps around a lot, and that can feel busy, but I don’t know if that’s the same as worry.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or following through to finish them?

Yeah, that one is… yeah. My apartment kind of looks like a bunch of things I meant to finish all at once. Like rent papers on the table, gallery notes in one pile, random article PDFs open on my laptop, and then three different to-do lists that don’t match each other.

I’ll start trying to sort it out and then I get stuck on what the first step is supposed to be. Like, do I answer an email first, or organize the notes, or read the article, and then somehow I’ve spent twenty minutes just moving things around. So I do follow through eventually sometimes, but organizing the steps is definitely hard.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work or school and at home?

Yeah, it’s not just one place. Like at home, my apartment is basically… I don’t know, it looks like everything is mid-thought. Rent papers on the table, notes from a gallery thing in a pile, random lists that don’t match.

And then on my laptop it’s the same version of that, just digital—article PDFs open, notes, tabs, to-do lists. I’ll sit down to start and then get stuck trying to figure out what actually comes first. Like I’ll mean to handle one thing and somehow I’m just rearranging documents or moving papers around. So, yeah, it shows up in more than one area, I think.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Restless like… physically? I’m not sure. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s bouncing off the walls or anything. I can sit through stuff, usually.

I mean, I might shift around or change positions, but sometimes chairs are just uncomfortable—like those plastic ones in lecture halls, they’re awful. I remember one classroom had these tiny desks attached to the side, and I spent more time trying to fit my notebook and coffee on it than… sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So, yeah, I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it as a big problem.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind and are hard to get rid of?

Unwanted thoughts… um, I’m not totally sure what counts. Like, I get random stuff stuck in my head sometimes, like a song lyric or remembering I forgot to do something, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

I wouldn’t say I have thoughts that feel, like, intrusive in a scary way or anything. Or—sorry, I’m thinking of this one time I couldn’t stop remembering an awkward thing I said after class, but I feel like everyone does that? So I guess I haven’t really noticed that as a big issue.
Do you ever check the same thing over and over, even when you already know it’s probably fine?

Um… checking over and over? Not really, I don’t think so. Like I might double-check if I locked the door sometimes, especially if I’m already halfway down the stairs and then I’m like, wait, did I actually do that or just think about doing it? But I don’t think I get stuck doing it again and again.

Actually, doors are weird because my apartment door kind of sticks, so sometimes you have to pull it to make sure it catches—sorry, that’s probably not what you mean. But no, I haven’t noticed any major repeated checking thing.
